courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

lectures.title: What is Hash Table? Why we need it?

cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to learn about hash tables.
Now there is actually a built in hash table in JavaScript which are objects.
And I'm going to explain them briefly at the end of this section.
But here we are going to go ahead and build our own hash tables.
Now what is hash tables.
Imagine you own a store where you are selling the various types of fruits.
And in this store you have a large number of shelves.
Each shelf is numbered, and you want to organize the fruits so that you can find them quickly without
having to search through all the shelves.
Think of each shelf in a store as a storage bin, where you can place the items, and each item you
want to store has a unique label or identifier, like a fruit name.
And we are going to put these items into shelves and decide which shelf item should go.
In most stores, they are using the software where it tells the user the shelf number where the fruit
should go.
So let's say in our case we have ten kilogram apples and we need to decide in which shelf we are going
to put it.
So as we said, we are going to do it based on the instruction or the software.
So what we will do over here is we are going to take the Apple and check in the instruction or the software,
and it's going to show that in which shelf it's going to go.
So in our case let's say we need to put them in shelf three.
Then if we have the next fruit which is for example mango, and we need to place it into the shelf,
we are going to check it one more time from the software.
So in this case let's say the shelf number from the software or instruction comes one.
So we are going to put it in the shelf one.
Now similarly in case of the hash table the function takes the item label and converts it to the specific
shelf number.
Now in case of hash tables we will have array like this which starts as index from zero.
And it continues like.
Now when it comes to the fruit example, let's say we are going to put apple one more time to this hash
table.
So take into account that in this case we are going to put in the shelf key and value pairs.
So in this case the key is Apple and value is ten.
So based on the hash table, we are going to access the cell, and from that cell we will access the
key and get the value of the item.
So let's say we want to identify how many kilograms apple we have in our shelves.
In this case we are going to use key to access the value.
So in this case how we are going to store this key value pair into this hash table.
So we are going to use the only key.
We are going to take Apple and pass it to the magic function.
And the magic function will use these characters and return us a number, which is going to be the index
number over here.
So in this case it is returning three.
So this means that we can take this key and value pair save it to the cell which is located at the index
of three.
So similarly if we have the next key and value pair in this case we have mango.
We are going to use mango and pass it to this magic function.
It's going to do some calculations and return the number.
So in this case it is one.
So we are going to take this key and value pair and put it to this cell where the index is one.
Now you might be interested how we are converting this string to the number.
So we are going to discuss this in our upcoming lectures here.
You just need to know that it is just a magic function which is taking the strings and converting it
to the numbers.
So this magic function determines where we are going to put the items.
Now we have inserted these strings using this magic function.
Now the question is if we want to read the data from this array.
For example how many kilograms apple we have, how we are going to do it.
So in this case also we are going to do the same approach.
We are going to take the key.
So let's say we are checking for mango.
So pass it to this key to this magic function.
And it's going to return the same number one.
And we are going to use one to access this cell.
And we are going to use the mango key to access the value of mango over here which is 15.
So with this way we can find the elements in this array very fast.
So in hash tables this magic function called hash function.
So the first property of this hash function is.
So if we take mango and pass it to this function it's going to return a number which is one.
Now we cannot take the one and pass to this hash function and get the mango.
In this case, this is not a load over here, because this is only one way you can just take the string
and based on that string you can get the number over here, but you cannot pass the same number to expect
the string that we passed over here.
So this is the first characteristic of the hash function.
Now the second property is they are deterministic.
What that means is if you run this mango through this equation it will produce the number one.
Now next time if you take the mango and run it one more time, it's going to always return one.
So it doesn't matter how many times you pass the same string, it's going to always return the same
number.
So these are the two important properties of the hash function.
Now you might be interested why we need hashing.
So let's say we want to develop an app in which the search operation is used heavily.
And we want our app to perform as fast as possible.
So in this case we are going to use the hash tables.
So hash tables performs better than other data structures in terms of search operation.
Now, if you look at the time complexity of search operations in other data structures, you can easily
see that in an array, if distorted, it's going to take all again.
If it is not sorted, it's going to take on time complexity in linked lists for searching any string,
it's going to take on time complexity.
When it comes to the tree, it's going to take all log n time complexity.
But when it comes to the hashing, in most times, if our hash function is optimized, in this case
it's going to take all one time complexity because our hash function calculates the index.
And by using that index, we can just straight away access any given cell of the array.
And we know that accessing the array cells based on the index takes all one time complexity.
So this is going to be the most efficient way.
Now to achieve the best performance of the search operation the hash function must have less collisions.
So you might be interested.
What is collision.
We are going to talk about it in our upcoming lectures.
So hopefully with this lecture you have understood what is hash tables and why we need them.
